patches.value: Let R=Z_(p), n=lambda+1, and e_i=y^i v/i! for 0<=i<=lambda. First prove these are a C-basis. Iterating [x,y]=h and [h,y]=-2y gives h(y^i v)=(lambda-2i)y^i v and, for 1<=i<=lambda, x(y^i v)=i(lambda-i+1)y^(i-1)v. Iterating the latter identity gives x^i y^i v=i! lambda(lambda-1)...(lambda-i+1)v. This scalar is nonzero in C and v is nonzero, so y^i v and e_i are nonzero (also e_0=v is nonzero). The h-eigenvalues alpha_i=lambda-2i are pairwise distinct: alpha_i-alpha_j=2(j-i) is nonzero in C for i!=j. For any relation sum_i c_i e_i=0, fix j and apply the operator product over k!=j of (h-alpha_k Id). Since h e_i=alpha_i e_i, this gives c_j product_{k!=j}(alpha_j-alpha_k)e_j=0, hence c_j=0; thus the e_i are linearly independent. There are lambda+1 of them and dim_C V(lambda)=lambda+1 by H004. If they did not span, adjoining a vector outside their span would give lambda+2 linearly independent vectors, contradicting that dimension. Thus they are a basis. Also y^(lambda+1)v, if nonzero, would be an h-eigenvector of eigenvalue -lambda-2 by the same h-y relation. This eigenvalue differs from every alpha_i, whereas in the established basis h is diagonal with eigenvalues alpha_0,...,alpha_lambda; a nonzero vector cannot be an eigenvector for another eigenvalue. Hence y^(lambda+1)v=0, and all higher y-powers vanish. The x-action stops at e_0 because xv=0, so higher x-powers on e_i vanish once their index would be negative. Iterating the relations therefore gives, for r>=0, X_r e_i=binom(lambda-i+r,r)e_(i-r) when 0<=r<=i and zero when r>i; and Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) when i+r<=lambda and zero when i+r>lambda. In each case the zero is the just-proved termination of the respective string, not an assumption about an undefined basis vector. In the valid ranges these formulas follow by dividing x^r y^i v and y^(i+r)v by r!i! and using the displayed factorial coefficients. Thus the divided powers have integral matrices in this basis. Put M_R=R tensor_Z M inside V(lambda). Admissibility implies the R-algebra generated by all X_r,Y_r preserves M_R.

Using the basis proved in S001, define E_ab by E_ab(e_b)=e_a and E_ab(e_t)=0 for t!=b. The divided-power formulas give Y_lambda X_lambda=E_lambda,lambda: X_lambda kills e_i for i<lambda and sends e_lambda to e_0, while Y_lambda sends e_0 to e_lambda. They also give X_(lambda-i)E_lambda,lambda=E_i,lambda, since X_(lambda-i)e_lambda=e_i, and E_lambda,lambda Y_(lambda-j)=binom(lambda,j)E_lambda,j, since Y_(lambda-j)e_j=binom(lambda,j)e_lambda and it vanishes on the other basis vectors before projection. Since 0<=j<=lambda<p, neither lambda! nor j!(lambda-j)! is divisible by p, so binom(lambda,j) is a unit in R=Z_(p); this includes lambda=0 (the empty factorial is 1) and p=2. Therefore every E_i,j belongs to the R-algebra generated by the divided powers and preserves M_R.

For the generator a of J from F001, the vectors a e_i form an R-basis of M_R by the direct-sum decomposition and J=Ra proved in S003. Define b_i to be the image of a e_i in M_R/pM_R and then its image under (M_R/pM_R) tensor_F_p K = M tensor_Z K; these b_i form a K-basis. The divided-power formulas at r=1 give x(ae_i)=(lambda-i+1)ae_(i-1), y(ae_i)=(i+1)ae_(i+1), and h(ae_i)=(lambda-2i)ae_i, with the first term zero at i=0 (because xe_0=0) and the second zero at i=lambda (because y e_lambda=0 as established in S001). These integral action matrices reduce to exactly x b_i=(lambda-i+1)b_(i-1), y b_i=(i+1)b_(i+1), and h b_i=(lambda-2i)b_i over F_p and K, with the same endpoint zero actions. A Z-basis of M and its reduction identify M_R/pM_R with M tensor_Z F_p. Since K has characteristic p, extension of scalars identifies (M tensor_Z F_p) tensor_F_p K with M tensor_Z K and preserves these operator matrices. Thus this is an L(K)-module basis and action correspondence; no assumption that the h-eigenvalues remain distinct modulo p is involved.

For each 0<=r<=lambda<p, r! is invertible modulo p, so X_r and Y_r on the reduced module are the respective nonzero scalar multiples 1/r! of x^r and y^r; for r=0 the scalar is 1. The matrix-unit identities from S002 persist after reduction: their coefficients binom(lambda,j) are nonzero modulo p, and the same identities hold as operators on the K-basis b_0,...,b_lambda corresponding to the characteristic-zero e-basis. Thus any K-subspace W invariant under x and y is invariant under every E_i,j. If w=sum_i c_i b_i is nonzero in W, choose i with c_i nonzero. For every j, E_j,i w=c_i b_j, so b_j belongs to W. Hence W is the whole module. The dimension lambda+1 is positive, so the module is nonzero. This proves irreducibility, including lambda=0 and p=2.
